anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine one specified appliance at every one of Wembley's 90,000 seats.
anchors.assumption: Use the published seating capacity as a fixed ensemble size. This does not describe attendance, ownership of appliances, or the stadium's electrical supply.

anchors.referenceLabel: an A380's 853 maximum certified passenger places
anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine an A380 arranged at its 853-seat certification limit, with one specified appliance at each place.
anchors.assumption: 853 is maximum certified seating, not typical airline seating or an actual flight's passenger count.
anchors.sourceNote: Airbus facts and figures, February 2022, page 3: maximum certified seating 853; the separate typical four-class configuration is 545.

anchors.referenceLabel: the Sydney Opera House Concert Hall's 2,664 in-the-round seats
anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine one specified appliance at each of the Concert Hall's 2,664 seats in its in-the-round arrangement.
anchors.assumption: Use the venue's maximum in-the-round seating, not its 2,102-seat stage-facing configuration or the entire Opera House capacity.
anchors.sourceNote: The venue page gives 2,664 in the round and 2,102 facing the stage.

anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine one specified appliance in each of Buckingham Palace's 775 rooms.
anchors.assumption: The total includes several kinds of rooms. Do not call these 775 bedrooms, residents, or existing appliances.
anchors.sourceNote: The Royal Household reports 775 rooms and separately enumerates state rooms, bedrooms, offices and bathrooms.

anchors.referenceLabel: 800 passenger places across the London Eye's 32 capsules
anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine all 32 London Eye capsules filled to 25 places each, with one specified appliance at every place.
anchors.assumption: 800 is a derived simultaneous capacity, not an observed passenger count or hourly throughput. Places do not imply literal seats.
anchors.sourceNote: The capsule manufacturer states 32 capsules and a capacity of 25 people per capsule: 32 x 25 = 800.

anchors.referenceLabel: a freshwater batch the size of Ocean Voyager's reported 6.3-million-gallon habitat
anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine a separate batch of freshwater occupying Ocean Voyager's reported water volume.
anchors.assumption: Use 6.3 million US gallons as a rounded nominal volume. The actual habitat contains saltwater; pure-water properties apply only to this explicitly imagined freshwater batch, never to its inhabitants or actual operating conditions.
anchors.sourceNote: Georgia Aquarium's dive information packet, page 5, reports 6.3 million gallons of saltwater. The SI digits encode conversion, not measurement precision.

anchors.referenceLabel: the Eiffel Tower at its reported total weight
anchors.fictionFrame: Imagine the Eiffel Tower's entire reported mass moving together at one speed.
anchors.assumption: The operator reports approximately 10,100 tonnes total, including more than the 7,300-tonne metal framework. An ideal kinetic-energy comparison does not assert that the structure could survive movement.
anchors.sourceNote: The operator distinguishes 7,300 tonnes for the metal framework from 10,100 tonnes total weight. Use the total consistently.

materialProperties.assumption: This is a property at the stated temperature and pressure. Treating it as constant over a temperature rise is an additional approximation.
materialProperties.sourceNote: Patek et al., Reference Correlations for Thermophysical Properties of Liquid Water at 0.1 MPa (2009), Table 8, page 9, row 298.15 K. DOI 10.1063/1.3043575.

materialProperties.assumption: Use this density to determine the mass of the initial freshwater volume at 25 degrees Celsius and 0.1 MPa.
materialProperties.sourceNote: Patek et al. (2009), Table 8, page 9, row 298.15 K: liquid-water mass density at 0.1 MPa.
